mixture-of-experts.d: An architecture in which a layer's FFN is replaced by many experts (small FFNs) and a router that picks a few of them per token. Total parameters grow with the number of experts; the cost per token grows with how many are chosen (top-k).

expert.d: One of the small FFNs of an MoE layer. In the three recipe models it is a SwiGLU with its own gate, up and down and width moe_intermediate_size (2048 in GLM and DeepSeek, 640 in Qwen).

roteador.d: A linear layer \( W_r \in \mathbb R^{E\times d} \) that gives one logit per expert for each token; a score function turns the logits into ratings and top-k picks which experts run. In the checkpoint it is usually called mlp.gate.weight.

funcao-de-score.d: Turns the token→expert affinity logit into a rating (scoring_func): softmax (Qwen; the ratings compete and sum to 1), sigmoid (GLM; independent ratings that saturate at 1) or sqrtsoftplus (DeepSeek-V4).

sqrtsoftplus.d: DeepSeek-V4's score function: \( s = \sqrt{\ln(1+e^{\ell})} \). It equals ≈ 0.83 at ℓ = 0, grows like \( \sqrt{\ell} \) for large logits and does not saturate the way sigmoid does.

norm-topk-prob.d: A config field that tells the engine to renormalize the scores of the k chosen experts so they sum to 1 before combining the outputs. With softmax, it is equivalent to applying softmax to the k chosen logits only.

routed-scaling-factor.d: The factor ρ, a fixed hyperparameter in config.json (neither learned nor stored in the weights), that multiplies the routed experts' weights after renormalization (2.5 in GLM and DeepSeek-V3, 1.5 in V4, 16 in V2 without renormalization). It sets the “volume” of the routed part relative to the shared expert and the residual; the kernel must apply it exactly.

shared-expert.d: An expert that runs for every token, bypassing the router (n_shared_experts in GLM and DeepSeek; Qwen has no such field, and the shared expert is implied by shared_expert_intermediate_size). It captures common knowledge and frees the routed experts to specialize. All three recipe models have one.

shared-expert-gate.d: In Qwen, the shared expert's output is multiplied by a scalar \( \sigma(\mathbf w_s\cdot\mathbf x) \in (0,1) \) computed per token (shared_expert_gate.weight [1, 2560], kept in BF16).

computacao-condicional.d: The idea of running only the part of the network that is relevant to each input. In MoE, each token computes only k of the E experts in each layer.

experts-finos.d: The strategy of using many narrow experts instead of a few wide ones (e.g., 288 × 2048 in GLM, 512 × 640 in Qwen). It multiplies the possible combinations of experts per token at the same cost.

camadas-densas-iniciais.d: The first layers of an MoE, which use a dense FFN instead of experts. In GLM, first_k_dense_replace: 3: layers 0–2 with width 12288. DeepSeek-V4 replaced these layers with hash-routed MoE.

colapso-de-roteamento.d: A rich-get-richer dynamic when training an MoE: popular experts get more gradient, improve and attract even more tokens, until a few of them do all the work.

aux-loss.d: A term \( \alpha\sum_i f_i P_i \) added to the training loss to penalize uneven load across experts (router_aux_loss_coef = 0.001 in Qwen and GLM). It balances the load, but touches the logits that define the weights. It has no effect on inference.

aux-loss-free.d: The DeepSeek-V3 lineage's balancing: a per-expert bias is added to the scores only to pick the top-k and is adjusted outside the gradient according to the load. The combination weights still come from the unbiased scores.

e-score-correction-bias.d: An [E] tensor in FP32 holding the aux-loss-free balancing bias, frozen in the checkpoint (GLM [288], DeepSeek [256]). DeepSeek's loader maps ffn.gate.bias to this name.

bias-vl.d: A second routing bias, per MoE layer, in DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, used for image-token rows (e_score_correction_bias_vl in vLLM). In the hash layers, image rows skip the table and use the top-6 of s + bias_vl.

roteamento-por-grupos.d: Splits the experts into n_group groups (typically one per node) and forces each token to choose experts from at most topk_group groups, limiting expert-parallel traffic. Used in DeepSeek-V2/V3; disabled in GLM (1/1) and absent in V4.

tid2eid.d: The “token id → expert ids” table of DeepSeek-V4's hash layers: [129,280 × 6] in int32. The row for the token's id says which 6 experts serve it; the weights still come from the gate's scores.

desbalanceamento-de-carga.d: An uneven distribution of tokens across experts in a step. Since inference does not drop tokens, it turns into time: very popular experts become large batches in prefill and, with expert parallel, the most loaded GPU delays the step.

despacho-moe.d: Reorganizing the (token, slot) pairs so that each expert receives a contiguous batch (sort by expert, count, permute) and then summing the weighted results back into each token's output.

item-de-plano.d: Unit of work in TensorFold's MoE dispatch: the triple (expert, first pair, count), with up to 16 (token, slot) pairs in decode and up to 64 in a prompt chunk. An expert with many rows becomes several items of the same kernel instead of going to a separate path.

fator-de-capacidade.d: A per-expert, per-batch token limit used in MoE training; the excess was dropped. Inference engines like vLLM do not drop tokens: every token gets its k experts.

swiglu.d: A gated FFN: \( W_{\text{down}}(\mathrm{SiLU}(W_{\text{gate}}\mathbf x)\odot W_{\text{up}}\mathbf x) \). Used in the dense FFNs, the experts and the shared expert of all three models; GLM and DeepSeek also clamp the activations with swiglu_limit = 10.
